memory_candidates.content: In this repo's .claude/ deployment model, target files for meta edits often exist as dual copies that must be updated together to survive sync: (1) core agents like general-research-hard-agent.md exist byte-identical at .claude/agents/ AND .claude/extensions/core/agents/ (edit both -- use `cp` after editing one to guarantee byte-identity); (2) cslib agents at .claude/agents/ are SYMLINKS into .claude/extensions/cslib/agents/ (edit the extension file only); (3) skill SKILL.md files exist at .claude/skills/ AND .claude/extensions/core/skills/ but may DIFFER (edit both, matching sections); (4) contract files at .claude/context/contracts/*.md are git-tracked canonical (NOT provided by core extension), while the lean extension bundles its own DIFFERING copies under .claude/extensions/lean/context/contracts/ -- new core contracts need a lean parity copy too if lean-only deployments should retain them; (5) .claude/context/index.json is git-tracked and maintained directly (no generate-index script; only validate-index.sh / validate-context-index.sh), and contract index entries are not all sourced from extension index-entries.json -- new contract entries need mirroring into the relevant extension's index-entries.json. Before any meta edit, check for a symlink (readlink) and a same-named extension-source copy. Also: `bash .claude/scripts/validate-context-index.sh` line-count mismatches are warnings (10% tolerance), not hard failures -- pre-existing domain/field errors elsewhere in index.json won't block a correctly-formed new entry, but always diff against a git-stash baseline before attributing pre-existing errors to your own change, since a naive `git stash` can transiently pull in other in-flight parallel agents' uncommitted edits across the whole working tree.

When strengthening a hard-mode (H-technique) contract that other domain agents specialize (e.g., H4 adversarial verification specialized by cslib's BibKey checks and lean's lean_hover_info checks), preserve the domain specialization by re-expressing it as a value plugged into a shared structural bar's column (e.g., the 'Verification Method' column of a Claim Verification Table) rather than deleting or generically rewriting the domain-specific mechanics. This keeps the contract structurally uniform across agents (grep-checkable table headers) while letting each domain agent's Stage 4.5 documentation show concretely which values that column takes for its domain.
